opening.storyBeat: Hello, explorers. I am Bussola, a small compass with a wobbly needle. Four travel powers—Curiosity, Wonder, Creativity, and Teamwork—have slipped from my points. No villain took them; I simply forgot how to notice. On this trip, three different eyes can help me remember. Every safe clue counts, and a grown-up may save or skip any clue.
opening.youngestAction: The youngest explorer taps Wake Bussola.
opening.familyOath: We stay together, look kindly, and let every explorer help. We stop when an adult says stop. Different clues, same team.
tutorialSteps: Meet Bussola and wake the compass.
Choose or swap Spotter, Detective, and Navigator.
Look up together, then let the parent confirm, save, or skip.

states.interrupted: Clue paused. Bussola will hold your place while the family does what it needs.
states.resume: Welcome back. Your clue is waiting exactly where you left it.
states.skip: Clue saved. Nobody is left behind.
states.manual: A grown-up confirmed this clue. Your team can keep moving.
states.retry: Try a different clue—or save this one.
states.offline: Bussola is offline, but every mission and fallback still works.
states.closedVenue: The place is closed. Use the outside or card version; entry is never required.
states.tiredLegs: Tired legs choose the short, seated, or manual version. That still counts.
states.badWeather: Weather changed the route, not the team. Choose the sheltered, indoor, or card version.
states.endingWithSkips: Every journey has different clues. Your team brought the compass home.
states.endingAllObserved: You noticed every planned clue, and all four compass powers are glowing.
states.mondaySilent: No story opens on Monday. Bussola rests and resumes on Tuesday.

chapters.title: The Wobbly Needle
chapters.openingBeat: Bussola can still point north, but its Curiosity point is dim. Before the car moves, the parent opens three seated clues. The children will notice change, pattern, and kind words while the driver keeps eyes on the road.
chapters.closingBeat: Country clues, safe patterns, and five kind words click into one compass point. Curiosity is glowing; Bussola sleeps through Monday and waits for Tuesday's city of water.

chapters.title: The City That Floats
chapters.openingBeat: Bussola wakes in a city where boats do street jobs and stone paths cross water. Wonder will return only if the team looks for a lion, reads a bridge, compares boats, and makes one quiet listening stop.
chapters.closingBeat: The winged lion, bridge pattern, working boats, and quiet clue show four ways to read Venice. Wonder glows without anyone needing to hurry, enter a venue, or stand near an edge.

chapters.title: The Maker Islands
chapters.openingBeat: Bussola's brass face has gone blank. Murano and Burano hold maker clues in glass shapes, travel symbols, bright homes, and lace stories. The family must notice respectfully and invent a pattern of its own.
chapters.closingBeat: A glass pattern, a parent-led lagoon route, and three clearly labelled Burano stories fill Bussola's face. Creativity glows because the team copied nothing fragile and made something new together.

chapters.title: The Teamwork City
chapters.openingBeat: Bussola reaches Verona with Curiosity, Wonder, and Creativity awake, but its needle pulls three ways. Roman arches, a famous literary tradition, the Adige, and whichever Friday route the parent chooses will test how three roles become one team.
chapters.closingBeat: The family combines different discoveries instead of chasing a perfect route. Teamwork aligns the four compass points, and every completed, manual, or saved clue belongs to the same adventure.

thursdayShortTrip.rule: Any Thursday car outing replaces the VER-03 afternoon block; it is never added as another scored mission.

candidatePairs.reason: Use for heavy rain or severe-weather closure; Children's Museum requires a parent booking check.

missions.title: Country Detective
missions.storyBeat: Bussola's first Curiosity cards have tumbled out of order. From their seats, the explorers can help without watching the phone. The parent will announce a safe clue—a flag, a language, or a sign—after the family reaches a new country. The Spotter notices, the Detective compares, and the Navigator orders the cards. Two clues are enough to steady the needle.
missions.objective: Notice two parent-chosen country clues while safely seated.

location.label: Moving car for children; parent setup before departure or at a safe stop

roles.action: Point to a flag, language, or road-sign clue chosen by the parent.
Say one way the two clues differ.
Place the parent-announced country cards in order.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Curiosity wakes when the team notices change together.

completion.retryLine: Look for one parent-chosen clue, or use the country cards.
completion.explanation: Flags, words, and sign styles can change across borders. The parent names the country; the children only compare visible clues.
completion.successLine: First border clue saved—Curiosity is waking.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent names the current country; no automatic border detection.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Not applicable; use printed/offline country cards.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use signs seen through the window or offline cards.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete fully seated or manually.

safety: Parent starts before driving or at a safe stop.
Driver: no screen; everyone stays buckled.

missions.title: Alpine Tunnel Hunt
missions.storyBeat: Bussola's needle is blinking in a dark-light rhythm. The route might include a tunnel, but the app never guesses which road the family takes. If the parent announces a tunnel, the Spotter signals the start, the Detective compares dark and light, and the Navigator keeps the count. If no tunnel appears, three pattern cards solve exactly the same clue.
missions.objective: Count a parent-announced tunnel or use the offline pattern cards.

location.label: Confirmed route feature or safe-stop fallback

roles.action: Show one finger when the parent announces a tunnel start.
Compare the bright and dark pattern cards.
Keep the team count; do not name a tunnel unless the parent confirms it.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Every safe count steadies Bussola's needle.

completion.retryLine: Try one dark-light-dark card pattern, or let the parent confirm one announced tunnel.
completion.explanation: This mission is deliberately route-neutral: a real tunnel counts only when the parent confirms it, and the offline pattern is equally valid.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent announces the feature; no route or proximity check.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Use the printed sequence light, dark, light; the child chooses dark next.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use the light-dark-light sequence if visibility is poor.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete seated with that one pattern match.

safety: Driver never looks at or touches the app.
No unbuckling, window leaning, flash, or exact-route promise.

missions.title: First Italian Words
missions.storyBeat: Bussola remembers five tiny tools that fit in no suitcase: kind Italian words. The youngest explorer matches each word to a gesture, the Detective pairs it with its English meaning, and the Navigator chooses one phrase for the family to use later. Nobody must perform for a stranger. A wave, a card match, or a quiet family practice all wake Curiosity's friendly voice.
missions.objective: Match five polite Italian words to meanings or gestures.

location.label: Car while seated or any quiet stop

roles.action: Match a greeting card to a wave.
Pair each phrase with its English meaning.
Choose one phrase the family can use later.

phrases.gesture: Make a rising-sun shape with both hands.
Place one hand over your heart.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Kind words give Curiosity a friendly voice.

completion.retryLine: Match one word to its English meaning or gesture; one match is enough.
completion.explanation: Ciao can mean hello or goodbye. The other four cards add a morning greeting, thanks, please, and a more specific goodbye.

fallbacks.noGps: Play anywhere.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue needed.
fallbacks.badWeather: Play indoors or in the car.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Use gesture-only matching.

safety: No child must speak to a stranger.
The parent reads the pronunciation aid; audio is never required.

missions.title: Find the Winged Lion
missions.storyBeat: Bussola has reached Venice, but Wonder is still hiding. A lion could help—yet this city asks its lion to carry wings. Stop in a safe public place and look up together. The Spotter finds the wings, the Detective chooses what makes the animal unusual, and the Navigator confirms the whole team can pause before the parent checks the answer.
missions.objective: Find a winged lion from a safe public position.

location.label: Any safely visible winged lion in Venice

roles.action: Point to the wings.
Choose what makes this lion unusual.
Confirm the team can stop safely before the phone returns.

choices.label: It has fins
choices.hint: Take another look above its back.

choices.label: It has wheels
choices.hint: Take another look above its back.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The winged lion of Saint Mark is a symbol of Venice.

completion.retryLine: Take another look. Find the shape above the lion's back.
completion.explanation: The winged lion represents Saint Mark and is one of Venice's best-known symbols. It can appear on carvings, flags, and signs.
completion.successLine: Lion found—Wonder has its first clue.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses any safely visible lion.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Use the answer cards and choose ordinary lion or winged lion.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use the answer cards; wings are the deciding clue.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete seated or manually.

safety: Stop together; parent holds the phone.
Do not cross or enter a crowd for a clue.

missions.title: Bridge Detective
missions.storyBeat: Venice keeps many paths connected with bridges, and Bussola wants a bridge fingerprint. Stop before the phone appears. The Spotter chooses an arch, step pattern, or material. The Detective compares it with a second detail. The Navigator and parent choose the safe side to stand on. The team is reading the bridge, not racing across it or leaning for a better view.
missions.objective: Compare two safe bridge details without leaning over a rail.

location.label: Any safe Venice bridge; Rialto fact appears only if relevant

roles.action: Point to one arch, step pattern, or material.
Compare two bridge details.
Choose the safe stopping side with the parent.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Rialto Bridge was built from 1588 to 1592 and remained the Grand Canal's only bridge until the nineteenth century.

completion.retryLine: Choose one arch, step, or material, then compare it with one more detail.
completion.explanation: Rialto's stone bridge was built from 1588 to 1592 and was the Grand Canal's only bridge until the nineteenth century.

fallbacks.noGps: Any bridge works.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Outdoor clue only; no venue required.
fallbacks.badWeather: Under shelter, compare the rounded-arch and pointed-arch cards.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Compare those two arch cards while seated.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Stay beside an adult and behind the rail; never lean, climb, run, or block the bridge.

missions.title: Boat Detective
missions.storyBeat: Bussola expected wheels, but Venice keeps showing boats with different shapes and jobs. From a safe place behind a barrier, the Spotter chooses one visible shape, colour-plus-icon, or movement. The Detective compares it with a second boat. The Navigator sorts the offline cards into people, parcels, or work clues. The parent—not the game—makes every real travel decision.
missions.objective: Compare two safely observed boats without choosing transport.

location.label: Safe waterside view behind a barrier or offline cards

roles.action: Point to a shape, colour-plus-icon, or movement.
Name one difference between two boats.
Sort the offline cards by people, parcels, or work clues.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Wonder grows when the team notices how a city works.

completion.retryLine: Compare one shape, icon, or movement—or match two offline boat cards.
completion.explanation: Boats can move people, parcels, supplies, or workers through a city built around canals. The mission asks only for observation, never a transport choice.

fallbacks.noGps: Any safe waterside view works.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Compare the long-low and short-tall boat cards.
fallbacks.badWeather: Sort the people, parcel, and work cards under shelter.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Compare two cards from a seat or complete manually.

safety: Stop walking, keep eyes up, and stay behind the edge or barrier.
Parent makes every real transport decision; do not follow a boat for a clue.

missions.title: Canal Sound Hunt
missions.storyBeat: Bussola's screen cannot collect this clue. First, stop somewhere safe; then the parent lowers the phone. For ten quiet seconds, the Spotter chooses a sound icon or visual card, the Detective compares near with far or steady with sudden, and the Navigator begins and ends the pause. Hearing is optional: three visual clues or imagined sounds restore Wonder just as well.
missions.objective: While stopped, notice three sounds or match three visual clues.

location.label: Any safe, stationary canal-side or quiet-space alternative

roles.action: Choose a sound icon or visual clue.
Compare near/far or steady/sudden.
Start and end the quiet ten-second pause.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Wonder can be heard, seen, or quietly imagined.

completion.retryLine: Choose one sound icon or visual clue; quiet mode is a complete answer.
completion.explanation: A city can be read through rhythm, movement, and changing distance—not only through words or pictures.
completion.successLine: Three careful clues collected—Wonder is glowing.

fallbacks.noGps: Play anywhere safe.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue needed.
fallbacks.badWeather: Under shelter, compare the ripple, bell, and footstep visual cards.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Play seated; one visual card is valid.

safety: Stop walking before the phone leaves the parent's hand.
Do not record strangers or require sound.

missions.title: Glass Pattern Lab
missions.storyBeat: Bussola's brass face needs its first maker mark. Murano is known for glass, but this mission needs no shop, furnace, or ticket. From a public place, the Spotter finds a repeated shape or reflection without touching anything. The Detective names what repeats and what changes. The Navigator arranges three cards into a new pattern. The family observes carefully, then invents its own design.
missions.objective: Find or build a three-part pattern without touching merchandise.

location.label: Murano public space, window display with permission, or offline cards

roles.action: Point to a repeated shape or reflection.
Explain what repeats and what changes.
Arrange three offline pattern cards.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Murano is known internationally for glassmaking workshops and artistic glass.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Murano's Glass Museum was founded in 1861.

completion.retryLine: Find one repeated shape or build a three-card pattern.
completion.explanation: Murano is internationally known for artistic glass, and its Glass Museum preserves island-made glass from across centuries. The team's new pattern is its own creation.

fallbacks.noGps: Any parent-selected Murano spot works.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Museum and furnace entry are optional; continue circle, star, circle with star.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use that circle-star pattern under shelter.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete the circle-star-circle pattern while seated.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Do not touch merchandise or workshop equipment; no photo is needed.

missions.title: Lagoon Navigator
missions.storyBeat: Bussola can read compass points, but not a lagoon timetable. While the family is stationary, the Spotter matches one stop symbol, the Detective compares stop, route, and direction labels, and the Navigator reads only the destination card chosen by the parent. These clues practise symbol reading. They never choose a boat, platform, departure, or boarding time; the parent checks the real journey.
missions.objective: Match stop and route symbols while stationary.

location.label: Stationary stop/waiting area or offline transit cards

roles.action: Match one visible stop symbol to its card.
Compare route, stop, and direction labels.
Read the parent-chosen destination card; do not choose the real service.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: ACTV water transport serves Venice and lagoon routes connect islands including Murano and Burano.

completion.retryLine: Match one stop, route, or direction symbol to its card.
completion.explanation: Venice's public water transport serves the city and connects lagoon islands including Murano and Burano. Only the parent uses current service information.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent selects the stop; no proximity check.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Match the stop dot, route line, and direction arrow cards.
fallbacks.badWeather: Match one of those symbols while sheltered and stationary.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Match one symbol while seated.

safety: Stop moving, keep eyes up, and stay together away from platform or water edges.
Parent checks the live service and makes every boarding decision.

missions.title: Colour-and-Lace Code
missions.storyBeat: Burano gives Bussola three beautiful clues that are not the same kind of truth. From a respectful public path, the Spotter matches two named colours with their shapes. The Detective sorts a FACT, a TRADITION, and a LEGEND. The Navigator chooses a stopping place away from homes and doors. Then the team links the colour pattern to a lace-like line without touching or photographing anyone.
missions.objective: Match a house pattern and separate fact, tradition, and legend.

location.label: Burano public path without blocking homes; offline alternative

roles.action: Match two named colours using their paired shapes.
Sort FACT, TRADITION, and LEGEND cards.
Choose a respectful stopping place away from doors with the parent.

facts.label: TRADITION
facts.text: People traditionally say bright houses helped returning fishers recognise home in fog.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The official source describes the rainbow practice as comparatively recent and connected with property boundaries.

facts.label: LEGEND
facts.text: A local tale imagines sea foam becoming a lace veil.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The Lace Museum occupies Burano's historic lace school founded in 1872.

completion.retryLine: Sort just one card by its printed label, or use the offline colour-and-shape pattern.
completion.explanation: The fishing-in-fog idea is a tradition, the sea-foam lace veil is a legend, and the official account links the more recent rainbow practice with property boundaries.

fallbacks.noGps: Any respectful public view works.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Lace Museum entry is optional; match blue-circle with yellow-star, then sort the three story labels.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use that colour-shape pair and label sort under cover.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete one label sort while seated.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Do not touch, enter, block, or photograph homes, doorways, or residents; colour clues always include shapes.

missions.title: Arena Time Machine
missions.storyBeat: Bussola's first Verona clue is older than every family member added together many times over. From a safe place in Piazza Bra, the Arena's outside arches become a gentle time machine. The Spotter finds one repeating arch, the Detective compares old stone with a modern event feature, and the Navigator chooses the viewpoint with the parent. The complete mission stays outside; no ticket or entry is needed.
missions.objective: Find a repeating arch pattern from Piazza Bra.

location.label: Arena exterior from a safe public position

roles.action: Point to one repeating arch shape.
Compare an old stone feature with a modern event feature.
Choose a safe viewing point with the parent.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The Romans built Verona's Arena around the middle of the first century AD.

completion.retryLine: Find one curved opening, then look for the same shape again.
completion.explanation: The Romans built Verona's Arena around the middle of the first century AD. Its repeating exterior arches make the history visible without entering.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent selects the exterior viewpoint.
fallbacks.closedVenue: The mission is complete outside; entry is never required.
fallbacks.badWeather: Under shelter, continue the arch, arch, gap pattern with arch.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Use that pattern from a seat or complete manually.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Keep arena history non-graphic and do not climb stonework.

missions.title: Juliet's Message Mystery
missions.storyBeat: Bussola has received a mixed-up message near Juliet's House. One card is documented building history, one explains how literature and tradition linked the house to Juliet, and one is Bussola's own fiction. The Spotter notices an exterior detail, the Detective sorts the labels, and the Navigator chooses a short or seated route toward Piazza Erbe. The courtyard and museum are never required.
missions.objective: Sort story labels, then carry one kind message toward Piazza Erbe.

location.label: Public route near Juliet's House and Piazza Erbe; no interior assumed

roles.action: Find a tower-house or square detail from the public route.
Sort FACT, TRADITION, and OUR STORY.
Choose the short or seated route with the parent.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The tower house is documented from 1351; its famous balcony was added during a 1939–1940 restoration.

facts.label: TRADITION
facts.text: The site's Juliet association developed after literary versions and later identification as the Capulets' house.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Piazza Erbe is Verona's oldest square and occupies the Roman forum area.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Bussola's mixed-up message is fiction made for this family quest.

completion.retryLine: Read the printed labels first: documented building, literary tradition, or Bussola's story.
completion.explanation: The house is historic, but its famous balcony is a twentieth-century addition. Its Juliet identity grew from literature and later tradition, not proof that the fictional character lived there.
completion.successLine: Message sorted: history and story can share a city without becoming the same thing.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses either site or uses the FACT, TRADITION, and OUR STORY cards.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Courtyard and house entry are never required.
fallbacks.badWeather: Sort the three label cards under shelter or at the hotel.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Sort just one labelled card while seated.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up; do not enter a crowd or block a doorway.
Do not touch the statue or leave a physical message; parent controls any booking.

missions.title: Cross the Adige
missions.storyBeat: The Adige bends through Verona, and Ponte Pietra offers five arches as the team's next code. From a safe approach or viewpoint, the Spotter points to each arch, the Detective compares two colours or materials, and the Navigator chooses with the parent whether to cross, view, or use the offline card. The clue never asks anyone to lean, hurry, or cross for points.
missions.objective: Count or match five arches from a safe position.

location.label: Ponte Pietra safe approach/view or offline bridge card

roles.action: Point to one arch at a time.
Compare two arch colours or materials using labels and shapes.
Choose cross, view, or offline mode with the parent.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Ponte Pietra spans the Adige with five arches and is open to pedestrians and bicycles rather than cars.

completion.retryLine: Count one arch at a time, or match the five-arch card.
completion.explanation: Ponte Pietra spans the Adige with five arches and is open to pedestrians and bicycles rather than cars.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent selects the viewpoint.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Outdoor public view or offline card.
fallbacks.badWeather: View from shelter or use the card.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Do not cross; count from a safe seat or complete manually.

safety: Stop walking, keep eyes up, and stay beside an adult behind the rail.
No leaning, climbing, or crossing for a clue; a Thursday car trip replaces this block.

missions.title: Excursion Morning Slot
missions.storyBeat: Friday's morning clue is sealed until the parent chooses a candidate pair. The mission ID and score never change. Wherever the family goes, the Spotter finds one shape or nature clue, the Detective explains a pattern or defensive feature, and the Navigator chooses the short route with the parent. If no destination is chosen, the team may use the card, confirm manually, or skip.
missions.objective: Complete the selected morning variant or resolve it manually.

roles.action: Find the selected variant's shape or nature clue.
Explain one pattern or defensive feature.
Choose the short route or manual mode with the parent.

variants.title: Sigurtà Team Maze
variants.locationLabel: Parco Giardino Sigurtà public visitor route or offline garden cards
variants.storyBeat: Bussola's morning needle points into a garden of choices. This is a no-rush team maze, even if the family never enters a maze. The Spotter finds one leaf, flower, or sign shape. The Detective identifies what repeats. The Navigator and parent select one marked path and the family stays together. A single pattern completes the clue; speed, distance, and reaching a centre do not matter.
variants.objective: Use one sign and one nature pattern to solve a no-rush team route.

roles.action: Point to one leaf, flower, or sign shape from the shared route.
Explain what repeats in the chosen pattern.
Read one parent-chosen sign and keep the team on one marked path.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: The park's current 2026 season includes 9 October, with October closing at 18:00 and last entry at 17:00.

completion.retryLine: Choose one nearby nature pattern; there is no finish line.
completion.explanation: The garden route is the clue: one repeated natural shape and one shared path are enough. The parent rechecks current opening and weather information.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses any marked path; no position check.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Sort the leaf, flower, and sign-shape cards or complete manually.
fallbacks.badWeather: Select the Verona rain pair, sort those cards, or skip; severe weather can close the park.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Use one card pattern or complete seated/manually.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Stay together; no running, maze separation, plant touching, or shortcutting.

variants.title: Castle on the Water
variants.locationLabel: Sirmione castle exterior from a safe public approach or offline card
variants.storyBeat: Sirmione's castle seems to grow from the water, but Bussola needs only an exterior shape code. From a safe public approach, the Spotter finds a wall, battlement, or harbour shape. The Detective matches it to the defensive-shape cards. The Navigator chooses the viewing point with the parent. Entry is optional, and no clue asks the team to approach an edge or squeeze through a crowd.
variants.objective: Match one wall, battlement, and water shape from the safe exterior view or cards.

roles.action: Point to one wall, battlement, or harbour shape.
Match that feature to a defensive-shape card.
Choose the exterior viewpoint with the parent.

facts.text: The fourteenth-century castle has walls, swallowtail battlements, walkways, and a harbour that sheltered boats.

completion.retryLine: Use the exterior card to find one wall top or harbour shape.
completion.explanation: The fourteenth-century Scaligero Castle includes swallowtail battlements and a fortified harbour once used to shelter boats.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses the viewpoint; no location check.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Match the wall, battlement, and harbour cards.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use those three cards or the Verona rain pair.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Match one feature from the nearest safe viewpoint or card.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Stay with an adult; no water-edge, climbing, or crowd-crossing clue.

variants.title: Indoor Pattern Rescue

variants.storyBeat: Rain has folded the outdoor map, so Bussola opens an indoor pattern case. If the parent chooses the museum, the Spotter points to one fossil, animal, or shape pattern without touching it. The Detective explains what repeats or changes. The Navigator chooses one room or ends the mission after one clue. If entry is unavailable, the three offline cards create the same rescue at the hotel.

roles.action: Point to one fossil, animal, or shape pattern without touching.
Explain one repeat or change in the pattern.

completion.explanation: The rain route tests the same Teamwork skill: three roles combine one observation without depending on entry.

fallbacks.badWeather: This is already the heavy-rain version.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Choose one seated pattern card or one nearby display, then finish.

Follow venue rules, stay together, and do not touch displays.

No running, maze separation, climbing, or water-edge clue.

missions.title: Excursion Afternoon Slot
missions.storyBeat: Friday's afternoon slot uses the partner clue from the parent's chosen pair. The Spotter finds one wheel, wall, water, or exhibit shape. The Detective labels one statement FACT, LEGEND, or OUR STORY. The Navigator chooses one clue and calls the block complete. The family never adds a second stop just for points; a card, manual confirmation, or skip protects the finale.
missions.objective: Complete the selected afternoon variant or resolve it manually.

roles.action: Point to the selected variant's water, wheel, wall, or exhibit shape.
Label one statement fact, legend, or our story.
Choose one clue only, then call the block complete.

variants.title: Water-Mill Mystery
variants.locationLabel: Borghetto public village route away from the river edge or offline cards
variants.storyBeat: Borghetto gives Bussola a clue with two labels. The old water mills and stone houses belong to documented place history; the Lover's Knot belongs to legend. Away from the river edge, the Spotter finds a wheel or stone shape, the Detective sorts FACT from LEGEND, and the Navigator chooses one short public view with the parent. The story works without eating, entering, or touching anything.
variants.objective: Find one mill shape and correctly label the Lover's Knot as legend.

roles.action: Point to a wheel, stone-house, or bridge shape from the safe route.
Sort the water-mill card as FACT and Lover's Knot as LEGEND.
Choose one short public viewpoint with the parent.

choices.label: The Lover's Knot is a legend
choices.hint: The source tells it as a local tale.

choices.label: The Lover's Knot is a building record
choices.hint: Take another look at the printed label on the tale card.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Borghetto preserves stone houses, old water mills, and the fortified Ponte Visconteo.

facts.label: LEGEND
facts.text: The Lover's Knot tale links local tortellini with Silvia, Malco, and a knotted silk cloth.

completion.retryLine: Take another look: the knot card is labelled LEGEND.
completion.explanation: Borghetto's mills and stone houses are physical place history. The tale of Silvia, Malco, and a knotted yellow cloth is a local legend.
completion.successLine: Mill fact and knot legend sorted.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses one safe public view; no proximity check.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue is needed; use the outdoor or card version.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use the cards under shelter or select the Verona rain pair.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Make one seated shape match and label the legend.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Stay with an adult away from the river edge; do not enter homes or touch mill equipment.

variants.title: Lazise Bonus Spotter
variants.locationLabel: Parent-selected Lazise public stop, parked-car cards, or skip
variants.storyBeat: After Sirmione, Bussola offers a bonus that is allowed to stay tiny. If the family stops in Lazise, the Spotter chooses one wall, window, or boat shape from a safe public place. The Detective turns it into a team symbol. The Navigator decides with the parent whether one clue is enough. If the day already feels full, the offline card or a skip completes the slot kindly.
variants.objective: Choose one safe visible shape and invent a team symbol, or use the offline card.

roles.action: Point to one wall, window, or boat shape from the shared stop.
Turn the shape into a simple team symbol.
Choose with the parent whether this one clue ends the block.

facts.label: FACT
facts.text: Lazise's public historic centre retains Scaliger walls and gates beside its old harbour.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: A short bonus clue can be enough after a long day.

completion.retryLine: Choose any one card shape; the bonus can end there.
completion.explanation: This is intentionally an OUR STORY activity, not a historical claim. Its purpose is to protect energy and make one shared symbol.
completion.successLine: One small clue became a team symbol.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses the stop or cards.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue is needed; choose circle, arch, or wave as the team symbol.
fallbacks.badWeather: Choose one of those shapes in the parked car, hotel, or under shelter.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Skip the stop or choose one seated shape; both resolve the slot.

safety: Stop walking and keep eyes up while the parent holds the phone.
Stay with an adult away from traffic and water; never add this stop when the family is tired.

variants.title: Indoor Team Spark
variants.locationLabel: Children's Museum only if already booked, or hotel/manual card mode
variants.storyBeat: Rain keeps the afternoon indoors, but Bussola needs no ticket to finish. If the parent has already chosen the museum, each explorer selects one safe hands-on discovery after using it. The Spotter points to its card, the Detective explains a change, and the Navigator joins three cards into one team sequence. Without a booking, the same three-card challenge works at the hotel.
variants.objective: Combine one discovery from each role at the chosen indoor place or with offline cards.

roles.action: Point to one parent-approved discovery or its card.
Explain one thing that moved, changed, or surprised the team.
Arrange three cards into one beginning-middle-end sequence.

completion.retryLine: Use any three offline cards to make a beginning, middle, and end.
completion.explanation: The indoor mission rewards a shared sequence, not venue entry. Hotel cards provide the complete equivalent.
completion.successLine: Three indoor clues made one team spark.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent chooses museum or hotel mode.
fallbacks.closedVenue: At the hotel, order the move, change, and surprise cards; entry is never required.
fallbacks.badWeather: This is already the heavy-rain version.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Order any two cards while seated or resolve manually.

safety: Stop moving before the parent uses the phone.
Follow venue rules, stay together, and use only parent-approved exhibits; no photo is needed.

completion.retryLine: Choose one clue from the selected variant, use its card, or resolve manually.
completion.explanation: The afternoon slot is intentionally one-clue-only. The selected pair changes content, never access to the finale.

fallbacks.noGps: Parent selects the variant and location manually.
fallbacks.closedVenue: Use public exterior/offline/manual mode.
fallbacks.badWeather: Select verona-rain or skip without penalty.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Lazise is optional; one seated observation or manual completion resolves the slot.

safety: Stay beside an adult near rivers and lakes.
Do not block homes, touch equipment, or add a second stop when the family is tired.

missions.title: Restore the Compass
missions.storyBeat: Bussola now holds Curiosity, Wonder, and Creativity, while Teamwork flickers at the centre. The finale works anywhere safe. The Spotter chooses one favourite discovery icon. The Detective labels it FACT, TRADITION, LEGEND, or OUR STORY. The Navigator places the four power cards around Bussola. When three different actions meet, the needle aligns—whatever route, weather, manual choices, or skips brought the family here.
missions.objective: Combine one action from each role and restore Teamwork.

location.label: Any safe Verona viewpoint, hotel, car while parked, or indoor place

roles.action: Choose one favourite discovery icon.
Say whether it was fact, tradition, legend, or our story.
Place the four power cards around Bussola.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: Different routes can restore the same shared compass.

completion.retryLine: Choose one discovery icon and one story label; the parent may place the cards.
completion.explanation: The four powers belong to the whole family. Resolved clues—including manual choices and skips—keep the finale open because teamwork is not a perfect score.
completion.successLine: Different route, same team. Teamwork is glowing.

fallbacks.noGps: Finale works anywhere.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue required.
fallbacks.badWeather: Use the static indoor celebration.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: Complete seated with no motion or sound.

safety: No public performance is required.
Skipped excursion slots never block this mission.

missions.title: The Home Arrow
missions.storyBeat: On Saturday, Bussola's needle points home. This is an epilogue, not a scored mission. Before driving, at a safe stop, or after arriving home, the Spotter chooses a favourite stamp, the Detective names one surprising discovery, and the Navigator points the offline arrow toward Basel. The compass keeps no route history; the family's retelling is what carries the journey home.
missions.objective: Choose one favourite clue to remember together.

location.label: Before departure, safe stop, or after arriving home

roles.action: Choose a favourite stamp.
Name one surprising thing.
Point Bussola's home arrow toward Basel on the offline card.

facts.label: OUR STORY
facts.text: The restored compass can carry memories without keeping a location history.

completion.retryLine: Choose just one stamp, or close the story with one tap.
completion.explanation: The home arrow is an offline story card. It does not use GPS, store a route, or add points.
completion.successLine: Home is the final direction, not a score.

fallbacks.noGps: Use the offline home arrow.
fallbacks.closedVenue: No venue required.
fallbacks.badWeather: Play in the parked car or at home.
fallbacks.tiredLegs: One tap closes the story.

safety: Parent starts before driving, at a safe stop, or at home.
Driver never uses the phone.
